record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Expansive Systems
record.context_brief: Approximation of expansive torus diffeomorphisms by Anosov maps
record.original_question: Let T^2 be the two-torus and let f: T^2 -> T^2 be an expansive diffeomorphism. Must f belong to the C^1-closure of the set of Anosov diffeomorphisms on T^2? Equivalently, is every expansive diffeomorphism of the two-torus a C^1-limit of Anosov diffeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: However, it is not known, whether the C1-closure of the C1-interior of the expansive diffeomorphisms of T2 includes all the expansive diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus. In other words: Is every expansive diffeomorphism the C1-limit of Anosov diffeomorphisms?
Open Problem 10.1: Does the C1-closure of the set of Anosov diffeomorphisms contains all expansive diffeomorphisms of the two-Torus?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ denote the two-dimensional torus, equipped with a Riemannian metric inducing a distance $d$. A diffeomorphism $f : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{T}^2$ is called expansive if there exists a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ (an expansivity constant) such that, for any two points $x, y \in \mathbb{T}^2$ with $x \neq y$, there is some integer $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $d(f^n(x), f^n(y)) > \varepsilon$. A diffeomorphism $f$ is called Anosov if there exists a continuous $Df$-invariant splitting $T\mathbb{T}^2 = E^s \oplus E^u$ of the tangent bundle, together with constants $C > 0$ and $0 < \lambda < 1$, such that for all $n \geq 0$, $\|Df^n|_{E^s}\| \leq C \lambda^n$ and $\|Df^{-n}|_{E^u}\| \leq C \lambda^n$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}^1(\mathbb{T}^2)$ denote the space of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^2$ with the $C^1$ topology, and let $\mathcal{A} \subset \mathrm{Diff}^1(\mathbb{T}^2)$ be the subset of Anosov diffeomorphisms. Determine whether every expansive diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^2$ belongs to the $C^1$-closure $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$ of $\mathcal{A}$; equivalently, decide whether every expansive diffeomorphism of the two-torus can be approximated in the $C^1$ topology by Anosov diffeomorphisms.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not produce a definitive resolution. While it is classically known (Hiraide, Lewowicz) that expansive homeomorphisms of closed surfaces of genus one are conjugate to Anosov diffeomorphisms, the differentiable question of whether every $C^1$ expansive diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^2$ lies in the $C^1$-closure of the Anosov diffeomorphisms is not clearly resolved in the available literature, and related recent works ($C^1$-generic continuum-wise expansive surface diffeomorphisms) treat genericity rather than full closure. The problem appears to remain open, but verification is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: C^1-generic continuum-wise expansive surface diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies C^1-generic properties of (continuum-wise) expansive surface diffeomorphisms; treats genericity within expansive systems but does not establish that all expansive diffeomorphisms on T^2 lie in the C^1-closure of Anosov diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies generic behavior of expansive surface diffeomorphisms in C^1 topology without resolving the closure question.

status_evidence.title: Anosov diffeomorphism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Anosov diffeomorphisms form a C^1-open subset of Diff^1; on T^2 every Anosov diffeomorphism is topologically conjugate to a hyperbolic toral automorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Background facts confirm structural stability and openness of Anosov, relevant to the closure question.
